data.narrative:
GRU is a private-stage company in Space & Aerospace founded by Skyler Chan. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, for a total of 13 sector peers.

Two standard triangulation methods are inapplicable here. Peer-median analysis fails due to insufficient narrow-stage clustering: while 14 same-sector peers exist, zero companies meet concurrent same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters simultaneously—the minimum threshold for reliable median anchoring is three datapoints. Public-comp anchoring likewise cannot proceed because GRU's revenue is not on file; the Space & Aerospace public median trades at 25.3x P/S across the six public tickers, but application requires disclosed revenue, which private companies rarely provide.

Without either peer-median triangulation or revenue-based multiples, this analysis cannot produce a quantified valuation range. A defensible estimate would require either: disclosure of GRU's revenue or EBITDA; identification of three or more private peers at identical stage and comparable scale with known valuations; or alternative methods such as DCF (requiring financial projections) or transaction comps from similar-stage capital rounds. The current data set supports only qualitative observation that GRU operates within a sector where public multiples average 25.3x sales, but this cannot be applied mechanically to an un-sized private target.
